review_note: Source says principle-oriented Tongliang likes active periods and can thereby express intelligence/talent; the effect is better modeled as activation/expression of cognitive capacity than generic 'environment fit'.
Source explicitly contrasts principle-oriented Tongliang external disputes/litigation under Xing-Ji with romantic Tongliang inner anxiety/psychological imbalance.
Source says Xing-Ji-clamped Tianxiang creates pressure; decisive Wuqisha handles it more calmly while short-sighted mode often ruins affairs.
Source says burdened Sun under bad Zipo has actions turn into '力不从心'; this is closer to execution/action capacity being constrained than an L3 outcome.
Source says principle-oriented Tongliang makes unburdened Sun labor more, while burdened Sun additionally risks planning errors; load state and downstream planning failure should be separated.
Source says yang/strong Tianji under turbulent Zipo can open a new situation; the canonical 'change-environment fit' is better treated as downstream constructive-change output.
Source explicitly says Qisha alone need not create change; Lu-Ma creates an objective environment in which passive Zifu has no choice but to change.
Source says only strong-will Taiyin is suited to Sha-Po-Lang periods and prefers Lu/Quan/Ke; strong will is a precondition, not an effect produced by the period.
Source says weak-will Taiyin under Sha-Po-Lang plus malefics becomes an adverse/degenerative change period; treat as temporal outcome, not a primitive-state increase.
Source says Wuqu Lu/Quan/Ke is an active favorable period for strong-will Taiyin and can produce '发足变泰'; downstream projection only.
Source says Tianji Hua-Ji is bad for any Taiyin and the more one seeks change the more trapped one becomes; encode a change gate/constraint plus downstream difficulty.
Source says Zifu periods favor strong-will Taiyin but produce inner contradiction in weak-will mode, especially with punishment/Ji.
Source says rash Tanlang dislikes Pojun periods and even Pojun Hua-Lu can be spoiled by rash action; downstream error/failure risk rather than a new primitive state.
Source says persistent Tanlang under Pojun Hua-Quan can take extra duties/new work and prosper; downstream developmental output.
Source says Qisha is relatively suitable for rash Tanlang, but heavy punishment/malefics create danger through misuse of authority; power-use relation and downstream trouble should be separated.
Source says persistent Tanlang can turn favorable after a period of difficulty in Jumen periods; keep as temporal transition/output pattern.
Source says rash Tanlang in Lianxiang may enjoy temporary glory and then fail from becoming carried away.
Source calls Tiantong with auspicious stars a constraining/settling period and says persistent Tanlang benefits most; environment-mode gate is more precise than a latent-state increase.
Source says Tanlang generally accomplishes something in a Wuqu year even without auspicious transformations; downstream achievement projection.
Source says Wuqu Hua-Ji requires even persistent Tanlang to avoid over-action, with rash mode needing stronger restraint; encode an action constraint rather than 'risk state'.
Source says impulsive Jumen in Tanlang periods has many disputes but can actively seek change; canonical 'impulsive fit' hides the simultaneous conflict cost.
Source says strong Lianxiang can withstand high-amplitude mixed good/bad periods and may turn adversity toward favorable outcomes; resilience remains derived/system-level after A1.
Source says fragile Lianxiang cannot cope with high-change/high-pressure environments and experiences intensified distress; separate compatibility mismatch from internal distress.
Source says Qisha periods suit shrewd Tianliang but upright Tianliang more easily attracts dispute unless strong auspicious support is present.
Source says Tiantong periods often establish a foundation for upright Tianliang, while shrewd mode must build through more hardship.
Source says good Wuqu lets shrewd Tianliang hold power but risks superior jealousy, while upright mode is trusted/valued; power position, support relation and outcome differ.
Source says Pojun generally favors shrewd Tianliang; upright mode should preserve integrity and be conservative.
Source says Wuqu Lu/Quan is auspicious for fulfilled Tiantong and can be especially prosperous; downstream projection only.
Source says exalted Sun with auspicious factors benefits both Tiantong modes and can temporarily make empty Tiantong active/enterprising; activation and downstream gain should be separated.
Source explicitly says Tianji Hua-Quan gives any Tiantong power like a machine receiving motive force; this is direct action-drive activation evidence.
Source says Tianji Hua-Ji is disliked by either Tiantong mode and one should not seek change but keep the old course; encode as change gate/constraint.
Source says Zifu is internally contradictory but still stable and therefore especially suitable for empty Tiantong; compatibility/stability environment is more precise than a primitive state change.
Source says Tanlang Hua-Lu stimulates Wuqu toward initiative and can mark leaving home/change of fate; separate action-drive activation from migration/life-course output.
Source says Pojun periods are important for Wuqu and enterprising Wuqu likes Pojun Hua-Lu; downstream opportunity/benefit.
Source says Tianji periods are liked by enterprising Wuqu; downstream opportunity rather than a new L1 state.
Source explicitly says Wuqu should actively seek change in Qisha periods, with punishment/malefics obstructing the change; direct change-activation plus gate.
Source says active Sun likes Pojun periods and can proactively improve the environment; downstream constructive-change projection.
Source says Tanlang is generally a good period for active Sun and brings favorable change; downstream projection.
Source says bad Lianxiang brings pressure/obstruction, while passive Sun can reduce pressure by accepting circumstances; this is a derived coping/compatibility relation, not a primitive state.
Source says active Sun in a Wuqu period can become emotionally unstable; if this changes its active nature toward yielding to fate, later periods are affected.
Source is more specific than 'environment repair': good Sha-Po-Lang/Kui-Yue conditions can transform reckless Pojun's purposeless destruction into purposeful construction, directly supporting QI-16.
Source says reckless Pojun under Qisha with malefics only knows removing the old and not establishing the new; direct evidence of low constructive goal-directedness.
Source says Tianji Hua-Ji can paradoxically be a good period for reckless Pojun, but whether it is used well becomes a key determinant of later development.
Source says Wuqu Hua-Ji activating Tanlang Hua-Ji is not a good period and neither Pojun mode should take aggressive action; encode a behavioral/action gate.
Source says auspicious Lianpo brings major gain to discerning Jiliang, while sharp mode labors much for little benefit.
Source says discerning Jiliang with Lianzhen Hua-Ji and CaYin-clamped Tianxiang can benefit by leaving the native place; migration output.
Source says discerning Jiliang meeting Xing-Ji-clamped Tianxiang mainly experiences work pressure; 'institutional pressure' is broader than the source.
Source explicitly gives a case where natal Tianji-Hua-Ke harmony is disrupted by transit Tanlang Hua-Ji, producing conflict/competition and loss from excessive self-reliance.
Source says good Tianxiang can let sharp Jiliang create something, but it must preserve gains and avoid over-extension; opportunity plus stability constraint.
Source says auspicious Tianxiang is a direct rise/development opportunity for discerning Jiliang.
